completeness.reason: REQ_SOC_ACCURACY's obligation is engaged only through the counting arm and only qualitatively - there is no share of the 3 % error budget allocated to current-measurement offset/quantisation drift, and no statement of how counted charge becomes a percentage of rated capacity.
completeness.suggestion: Allocate this element's slice of the 3 % accuracy budget explicitly (e.g. maximum tolerated integration drift per hour given the shunt's offset error) so the numeric obligation has a design-level counterpart.

consistency.reason: Cleanly reconciled with its sibling ARCH_OCV_CORRECTOR on REQ_SOC_ACCURACY: this element explicitly holds no absolute reference and defers the anchor to the corrector, which in turn reports anchor plus this counter's delta.

design_clarity.reason: Names the concrete choices instead of the goal: trapezoidal integration, a fixed 10 ms tick, ampere-second accumulation in a 64-bit fixed-point accumulator, and the two values it exposes.

implementability.reason: Realisable, but the current input is loose: ARCH_CURRENT_PATH_MONITOR samples pack current at 1 ms while this element integrates on a 10 ms tick, and the element does not say whether a tick consumes the latest sample or the mean of the ten - a choice that materially affects drift. Behaviour on a missing current sample is also unstated.
implementability.suggestion: Say which current value each 10 ms tick integrates (latest 1 ms sample vs mean of the ten), and what the accumulator does when no valid current sample is available for a tick.

parent_fit.reason: Substantively owns a distinct part of REQ_SOC_ACCURACY - the relative charge integral whose drift the accuracy band is spent on - and its representation choices (A.s, 64-bit fixed point) are argued in terms of not losing resolution.

summary: The numeric core is well chosen and precisely stated, and the split against ARCH_OCV_CORRECTOR is clean. What is missing is any engagement with the 3 % error budget it is supposed to serve, and the relationship between its 10 ms tick and the 1 ms current sampling upstream.
